item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-17: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “We have two senators-elect who would not be there if the current majority leader had his way” Unsettled. Reporting conflicts on whether Sen. Schumer publicly endorsed Rep. Haley Stevens against Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan (one outlet says he endorsed her; another says leadership had only a private preference). In Minnesota no public backing of Peggy Flanagan's opponent by Schumer, the DSCC or Senate Majority PAC was found, only reports of a private preference. Figures are as reported by news outlets; no official record covers private preferences.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-15: 1 contradicted (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “Republicans in Washington raised twice as many funds.” Contradicted. AskAmerica's Federal Election Commission data for the 2026 cycle show the three Republican national party committees with receipts of $843.1 million (RNC $341.5 million, NRCC $263.8 million, NRSC $237.8 million) against $725.5 million for the three Democratic committees (DNC $252.3 million, DCCC $256.8 million, DSCC $216.4 million): about 16 percent more, not twice. The FEC's own 18-month summary gives the same ratio. Still open: super PACs and other outside groups, which were not counted.

36 statements by 11 officeholders. 12 checked: 3 supported, 7 unsettled, 1 unsupported, 1 contradicted · 24 not checkable.
